contentMarkdown:
If you have ever needed a product photo without its background, a headshot on a clean canvas, or a sticker cut out of a photo, you have probably used remove.bg. Its standalone site shuts down on December 1, 2026, at 9:00 AM CET — and everyone who uses it needs a new home. Here is what the shutdown actually means, and a free alternative you can switch to today.

## What is actually shutting down

remove.bg is folding its background-removal feature into Canva, which has owned the technology since 2021. The standalone website — the simple "upload, cutout, download" flow everyone knows — will no longer be available after the cutoff. Unused pay-as-you-go credits expire that morning, and the Photoshop plugin and other integrations are being discontinued. Enterprise API contracts are not affected, but everyone else needs a plan before December.

One detail worth knowing: remove.bg's free downloads were always previews, capped at about 0.25 megapixels (roughly 625 x 400). Full-resolution downloads cost credits. So if you are looking for a genuinely free replacement, the fair comparison is free, full-size output, no credits — not just "free to try."

## The free alternative: remove backgrounds in your browser

The [free Background Remover](/tools/background-remover) does the same core job — upload a photo, get a transparent-background PNG — with one big architectural difference: the AI model runs inside your browser, on your device. Your photo is never uploaded to a server, and there is no account, no credit system, and no watermark.

Here is how to use it:

1. Open the [free Background Remover](/tools/background-remover).
2. Drop in a JPG, PNG, or WebP image (up to about 10MB).
3. On your first visit, the browser downloads the AI model (about 85MB) once — this takes a little while, and afterwards it is cached, so every later removal starts almost instantly.
4. The tool detects your subject and erases the background behind it.
5. Compare the before and after side by side, then download the transparent PNG.

Because everything happens on-device, it is private by design: sensitive product photos, client work, or personal portraits never leave your machine.

## An honest comparison

What remove.bg did well: one-click simplicity, fast turnaround, and a polish honed over years. A browser-based AI can match the core result — a clean cutout — but you should know the tradeoffs:

- **The first run is slower.** That one-time ~85MB model download is the price of privacy. Everything after it is instant.
- **Chromium browsers are fastest.** Chrome, Edge, and Brave get the best speed thanks to the hardware acceleration the model uses; Firefox and Safari generally work but can be slower.
- **Edge quality varies, like any automatic tool.** Clear subjects — people, products, pets — against distinct backgrounds give the cleanest cutouts. Fine hair strands, glass, and very busy backgrounds can leave rough edges that need a manual editor. If an image is too large, shrink it first with the [Image Compressor](/tools/image-compressor) or resize it with the [Image Resizer](/tools/image-resizer).

What you do not get: a credit balance, a paywall between you and full resolution, or your photos sitting on someone else's server. For everyday cutouts — product listings, profile pictures, thumbnails, design mockups — that is the part that matters.

## Switch before December 1

If you are still using remove.bg, do three things now: export any cutouts and account records you need, check your remaining credits (they expire on December 1), and try the free alternative above on your real images while you still have a fallback. When the standalone site goes dark, you will already have moved.
